name: One Acre Fund (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The locations the sheet's bottom line reads (row labels naming Rwanda, Kenya, Malawi, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Uganda), sharing equally.

missing_data.note: Measured: One Acre Fund counts the farmers it serves and measures their extra profit every season against matched non-clients, weighing sampled harvests.

summary: One Acre Fund sells smallholder farmers in East Africa and beyond seed and fertiliser on credit, with training and delivery, and runs shops, tree-seedling and extension programmes with governments. The Life You Can Save puts its return at 4.43 dollars of extra farm profit per dollar, from One Acre Fund's own 2024 measurement against matched non-clients and its net cost per farmer. Our view values a season's extra profit as a rise in the household's consumption, the site's way; the biggest uncertainties are the profit measurement itself and the share of the partnerships' results that is One Acre Fund's.

rows.explainer: One Acre Fund's own impact measurement: each season it weighs a random sample of clients' and comparable non-clients' harvests (matched on their characteristics), values them at market prices and subtracts all farm costs, inputs and loan interest included; trees, solar lights and other products add their net present value per client. The sheet calls the organisation-wide figure a weighted average.

Farmers reached in the countries with a consumption survey
rows.formula: clients_rwanda + clients_kenya + clients_malawi + clients_tanzania + clients_ethiopia + clients_uganda
rows.explainer: Rwanda, Kenya, Malawi, Tanzania, Ethiopia and Uganda: 87% of the farmers. The World Bank has no recent survey mean for Burundi or Nigeria, so their farmers take the others' mix.

rows.label: Consumption per person, Rwanda, 2024 (US$)
rows.explainer: The World Bank's household-survey mean for Rwanda, carried to 2024 and to nominal dollars (facts: survey_consumption), the shared baseline for the people a programme there serves (normalization 2.14).

rows.label: Consumption per person, Kenya, 2024 (US$)
rows.explainer: The World Bank's household-survey mean for Kenya, carried to 2024 and to nominal dollars (facts: survey_consumption), the shared baseline for the people a programme there serves (normalization 2.14).

rows.label: Consumption per person, Malawi, 2024 (US$)
rows.explainer: The World Bank's household-survey mean for Malawi, carried to 2024 and to nominal dollars (facts: survey_consumption), the shared baseline for the people a programme there serves (normalization 2.14).

rows.label: Consumption per person, Tanzania, 2024 (US$)
rows.explainer: The World Bank's household-survey mean for Tanzania, carried to 2024 and to nominal dollars (facts: survey_consumption), the shared baseline for the people a programme there serves (normalization 2.14).

rows.label: Consumption per person, Ethiopia, 2024 (US$)
rows.explainer: The World Bank's household-survey mean for Ethiopia, carried to 2024 and to nominal dollars (facts: survey_consumption), the shared baseline for the people a programme there serves (normalization 2.14).

rows.label: Consumption per person, Uganda, 2024 (US$)
rows.explainer: The World Bank's household-survey mean for Uganda, carried to 2024 and to nominal dollars (facts: survey_consumption), the shared baseline for the people a programme there serves (normalization 2.14).

rows.label: People in a farmer's household, by where the farmers are
rows.formula: (clients_rwanda * @household_size.rwanda_rural + clients_kenya * @household_size.kenya_rural + clients_malawi * @household_size.malawi_rural + clients_tanzania * @household_size.tanzania_rural + clients_ethiopia * @household_size.ethiopia_rural + clients_uganda * @household_size.uganda_rural) / clients_with_survey
rows.explainer: The shared rural household sizes from the Demographic and Health Surveys (facts: household_size), weighted by the farmers reached in each country.

rows.label: Consumption of a farmer's household, 2024 (US$)
rows.formula: (clients_rwanda * @household_size.rwanda_rural * baseline_pp_rwanda + clients_kenya * @household_size.kenya_rural * baseline_pp_kenya + clients_malawi * @household_size.malawi_rural * baseline_pp_malawi + clients_tanzania * @household_size.tanzania_rural * baseline_pp_tanzania + clients_ethiopia * @household_size.ethiopia_rural * baseline_pp_ethiopia + clients_uganda * @household_size.uganda_rural * baseline_pp_uganda) / clients_with_survey
rows.explainer: Household size times consumption per person in each country, weighted by the farmers reached there.

rows.label: Rise in ln(consumption) per household member from a season's extra profit
rows.explainer: The extra profit spread over the household's consumption for the year: the site values income gains as changes in ln(consumption). The profit is taken as consumed (some is saved and consumed later, which the shared rate treats alike).

rows.label: Years from spending to the harvest's extra profit
rows.explainer: Our judgment: inputs are delivered before planting and the gain comes at harvest, within the year.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the harvest
Share of the extra profit that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: ×1: One Acre Fund's figure is already measured against matched non-clients, so it is the gain over what would have happened anyway.

rows.label: One Acre Fund's share of the resources behind the gains
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 85% (60% to 100%), used only with credit by share of resources on. In partnerships governments and other partners pay for extension staff, shops and seedlings alongside One Acre Fund's 5.40 dollars a farmer; farmers' own costs are already netted out of the profit. We haven't seen the partners' spending.

rows.label: Deaths averted by higher incomes, as a share of the consumption benefit
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: aid_value): higher household incomes avert some child deaths; multiplied by the value-of-a-life slider. The sheet counts income only.

rows.label: Benefits beyond the season's profit, as a share of it
rows.explainer: A side effect, our judgment 10% (0 to 30%): practices farmers keep after they stop buying from One Acre Fund, better diets from bigger harvests, and the trees' soil and carbon benefits beyond what the farmer sells. The sheet counts the farmer's profit only.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of programme cost
rows.explainer: The shared default for programmes where staff deliver the help themselves: One Acre Fund's net cost is mostly its field officers, who train and serve the farmer groups.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: The shared default for delivery staff hired locally.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Full cost per dollar of the sheet's cost
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources on, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost. The sheet's organisation-wide cost per farmer already includes central costs (it is about twice the country programmes' own), so none is added.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.formula: household_size * ln_gain_per_person * $uov_per_ln_consumption * wait_discount * counterfactual_share * if($resource_shares, oaf_resource_share, 1) * (1 + income_mortality_uov_ratio * $life_value_multiplier + other_benefits_share) / (cost_per_client * cost_multiplier)
rows.explainer: A season's extra profit for a farmer's household, valued like every income gain on the site, with the deaths higher incomes avert and the benefits beyond the profit, per dollar of One Acre Fund's full cost.
